questions.why: Systolic pressure is the peak pressure in the arteries when the ventricles contract and eject blood.
questions.deep: Diastolic pressure (the bottom number) is the lowest pressure, when the ventricles relax and fill. Systole = squeeze, diastole = dilate/relax.

variants.stem: What is the main role of bicarbonate released by the pancreas into the duodenum?
Pancreatic bicarbonate raises the pH of chyme entering the small intestine. Its function is to:
Why does the pancreas secrete bicarbonate into the small intestine?

Pancreatic juice contains bicarbonate. What does it do?
What does bicarbonate do to the acidic chyme that enters the duodenum?
The alkaline bicarbonate in pancreatic secretions serves to:
In the duodenum, bicarbonate from the pancreas is needed to:

questions.why: Bicarbonate neutralizes the acidic chyme from the stomach so pancreatic enzymes can work at their optimal, near-neutral pH.
questions.deep: Pancreatic enzymes: lipase (fats), proteases such as trypsin (proteins), pancreatic amylase (carbohydrates). The bicarbonate itself is not a digestive enzyme.

variants.stem: Which structure attaches muscle to bone?
Muscles transmit force to bones through which structure?

Which connective tissue joins skeletal muscle to the periosteum of bone?
When a muscle contracts, it pulls on a bone via which structure?
Unlike ligaments, which structure connects muscle to bone?
What anchors a muscle to a bone?

questions.why: Tendons attach muscle to bone; ligaments attach bone to bone.
questions.deep: Memory aid: Tendons = muscle to bone ('T' for 'tug'); Ligaments = bone to bone ('L' for 'link' at a joint). Cartilage cushions joints; fascia wraps and separates muscles.

variants.stem: Which hormone surge triggers ovulation?
A sudden rise in which hormone causes the release of the egg from the ovary?
Ovulation is triggered by a mid-cycle surge of:
Which pituitary hormone causes the mature follicle to rupture and release an oocyte?
In the menstrual cycle, which hormone peaks just before ovulation and initiates it?
Which hormone is responsible for causing the ovary to release an egg?
A test strip that predicts ovulation detects a rise in which hormone?
Which hormone's surge is the signal for ovulation to occur?

questions.why: A surge of luteinizing hormone (LH) from the anterior pituitary triggers ovulation.
questions.deep: FSH stimulates follicle growth early in the cycle. After ovulation the follicle becomes the corpus luteum, which secretes progesterone. Prolactin stimulates milk production.

variants.stem: Which structure carries urine from the kidney to the urinary bladder?
Urine travels from each kidney to the bladder through which tube?
A kidney stone blocking the tube between the kidney and bladder is lodged in the:
Which structure transports urine from the renal pelvis toward the bladder?
Peristalsis moves urine through which narrow muscular tube leading to the bladder?
Which part of the urinary system connects the kidney to the bladder?
Urine leaves the kidney through which duct on its way to the bladder?
Which structure links the renal pelvis to the urinary bladder?

questions.why: The ureters carry urine from the kidneys to the bladder.
questions.deep: Urine path: nephron → collecting duct → renal pelvis → ureter → bladder → urethra → outside. Ureter = to the bladder; urethra = out of the body.

variants.stem: During inhalation, pressure inside the lungs is ______ the pressure of the atmosphere.
For air to flow into the lungs, the intrapulmonary pressure must be ______ atmospheric pressure.
When the thoracic cavity expands, the pressure in the lungs becomes ______ atmospheric pressure.
Air flows into the lungs because the pressure in the lungs is ______ the pressure outside the body.
As the diaphragm contracts and the lungs expand, alveolar pressure is ______ atmospheric pressure.
At the moment inspiration is occurring, lung pressure compared with atmospheric pressure is ______.
Boyle's law explains that when lung volume increases, lung pressure ends up ______ atmospheric pressure.
Inhaled air moves down its pressure gradient, which means lung pressure is ______ atmospheric pressure.

questions.why: Expanding the thoracic cavity increases lung volume, which lowers lung pressure below atmospheric pressure, so air flows in.
questions.deep: Boyle's law: pressure and volume are inversely related at constant temperature. During exhalation the volume decreases, pressure rises above atmospheric, and air flows out.

variants.stem: Where do T lymphocytes mature?
Which organ is responsible for the maturation of T cells?

questions.why: T cells mature in the thymus, where they learn to distinguish self from non-self.
questions.deep: B cells mature in bone marrow. The spleen filters blood and stores immune cells; lymph nodes filter lymph and host immune responses.

variants.stem: Which of the following are part of the appendicular skeleton? Select all that apply.
Select every bone that belongs to the appendicular skeleton.
Which options are bones of the limbs or the girdles that attach them? Select all that apply.
Identify all appendicular bones from the list.

Select all bones that form part of the limbs or the pectoral and pelvic girdles.
Which of the following belong to the appendicular skeleton rather than the axial skeleton? Select all that apply.
Choose every appendicular bone.

questions.why: The humerus, femur, and scapula are appendicular bones; the sternum and vertebrae belong to the axial skeleton.
questions.deep: Appendicular = limbs plus pectoral (scapula, clavicle) and pelvic girdles. Axial = skull, vertebral column, ribs, and sternum.

variants.stem: During which phase of mitosis do chromosomes line up along the cell's equator?
In which mitotic phase are the chromosomes arranged in a single line across the middle of the cell?
Spindle fibers attach to the centromeres and align the chromosomes at the center of the cell during:

At which stage are duplicated chromosomes positioned along the cell's equatorial plane?
Chromosomes are most easily counted under the microscope when they are lined up in the middle of the cell, during:
Which phase ensures each daughter cell will receive one chromatid from each chromosome by lining chromosomes up at the center?
The cell's chromosomes are arranged along its midline in which phase of mitosis?

questions.why: Chromosomes align along the cell's equator (the metaphase plate) during metaphase.
questions.deep: Order: Prophase → Metaphase → Anaphase → Telophase (then cytokinesis). Memory aid: PMAT. Metaphase = Middle; Anaphase = Apart.

variants.stem: Which of the following human cells is haploid?
Which cell type contains only 23 chromosomes?
Which of these cells carries a single set of chromosomes?
Which cell is a gamete?
Which of the following is NOT a diploid somatic cell?
Which cell results from meiosis rather than mitosis?
Which cell has half the normal number of chromosomes found in body cells?
Which of these is a germ cell rather than a somatic cell?

questions.why: Sperm cells are gametes, which are haploid (23 chromosomes). The others are diploid somatic cells (46).
questions.deep: Somatic cells make up the body and divide by mitosis. Germ cells give rise to gametes through meiosis. Fertilization restores the diploid number.

variants.stem: A nonsense mutation results in which of the following?

A single base change turns a normal codon into a stop signal. This results in:

Which result describes a nonsense mutation?
Which is a consequence of a nonsense mutation in the middle of a gene?

questions.why: A nonsense mutation changes an amino-acid codon into a stop codon, ending translation early.
questions.deep: Missense = changes one amino acid; silent = no change in the amino acid; nonsense = premature stop; frameshift = insertion or deletion shifts the reading frame.

variants.stem: Which term describes an organism that obtains energy by consuming other organisms?
Animals, fungi, and many bacteria that cannot make their own food are called:
An organism that must eat other organisms or organic matter for energy is a(n):

Which type of organism cannot produce its own food from inorganic sources?
Which term applies to organisms that rely on other organisms for their organic molecules?
What is a consumer's nutritional category?
Which nutritional mode describes organisms that obtain carbon from other living things?

questions.why: Heterotrophs obtain energy and carbon by consuming other organisms or organic matter.
questions.deep: Autotrophs (producers) make their own food using light (photoautotrophs) or chemicals. Hetero = other, auto = self, troph = feeding.

variants.stem: A human body cell has 46 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in each sperm or egg cell? Type a number.
How many chromosomes does a normal human gamete contain if a somatic cell has 46? Type a number.
Meiosis halves the chromosome number. If a human somatic cell has 46 chromosomes, how many does each gamete have? Type a number.

Each human gamete is haploid. How many chromosomes does it have, given a diploid number of 46? Type a number.

questions.why: Gametes are haploid, so they carry half of 46 chromosomes, which is 23.
questions.deep: Fertilization combines two gametes (23 + 23) to restore the diploid number of 46.

questions.deep: Enzyme activity rises with temperature up to the optimum, then drops sharply as the enzyme denatures (loses its shape). Always read the peak on the curve, not the end of the axis.

variants.stem: According to Le Chatelier's principle, adding more reactant to a system at equilibrium causes the equilibrium to shift:

questions.why: Adding reactant makes the system shift toward the products to use up the extra reactant and restore equilibrium.
questions.deep: Le Chatelier's principle: a system at equilibrium responds to a stress by shifting to counteract it. Adding product shifts the system toward the reactants.

variants.stem: According to the Arrhenius definition, a base releases which ion in water?
Which ion increases in concentration when a base such as NaOH dissolves in water?
Raising the pH of a solution means increasing the concentration of which ion?
Which ion do bases produce in solution?

Which ion is responsible for the bitter taste and high pH of basic solutions?
Compared with acids, bases produce an excess of which ion in water?
A substance that releases this ion in water is classified as a base. Which ion?

questions.why: Bases release hydroxide ions (OH⁻) in water.
questions.deep: Acids release H⁺ and lower pH; bases release OH⁻ and raise pH. Neutral water has equal amounts of each at pH 7.

variants.stem: The atomic mass listed on the periodic table represents which of the following?
The atomic mass of an element on the periodic table is best described as the:
Atomic mass values on the periodic table are calculated as the:

How is the atomic mass of an element determined?
An element's atomic mass on the periodic table is the:

questions.why: Atomic mass is the weighted average of the masses of an element's naturally occurring isotopes, which is why it is rarely a whole number.
questions.deep: The atomic number (a whole number) is the proton count. Chlorine's atomic mass is about 35.45 because roughly 75% of chlorine is Cl-35 and 25% is Cl-37.

variants.stem: According to the law of conservation of mass, the total mass of the products is ______ the total mass of the reactants.
In a closed system, the mass of the reactants is ______ the mass of the products.
When a chemical reaction occurs in a sealed container, the mass after the reaction is ______ the mass before.
Atoms are neither created nor destroyed in a reaction, so the mass of products is ______ the mass of reactants.
A balanced chemical equation shows that the mass of the products is ______ the mass of the reactants.
If 10 g of reactants fully react in a closed system, the mass of the products compared with 10 g is ______.
The law of conservation of mass states that total mass before a reaction is ______ total mass after the reaction.
Comparing total reactant mass with total product mass in a closed system, the product mass is ______ the reactant mass.

questions.why: Mass is conserved in chemical reactions, so total product mass equals total reactant mass in a closed system.
questions.deep: This is why equations must be balanced: the same number of each type of atom appears on both sides.

variants.stem: Which of the following are noble gases? Select all that apply.
Select every element that is in Group 18 of the periodic table.
Which options are elements with a full outer electron shell and very low reactivity? Select all that apply.
Identify all noble gases from the list.
Which of these elements are inert gases? Select all that apply.
Select all elements in the same group as xenon.
Which of the following elements rarely form compounds because their outer shell is full? Select all that apply.
Choose every noble gas.

questions.why: Helium, neon, and argon are noble gases (Group 18) with full outer shells. Nitrogen is Group 15 and chlorine is a Group 17 halogen.
questions.deep: Noble gases: He, Ne, Ar, Kr, Xe, Rn. Their full valence shells (2 for He, 8 for the rest) make them very unreactive.

questions.why: Qualitative data describe qualities (color, smell, texture) without numbers; quantitative data are measured numbers with units.
questions.deep: Qualitative = quality (words). Quantitative = quantity (numbers). Good lab notebooks record both.

questions.why: The readings are close to one another (precise) but far from the true value of 10.0 g (not accurate).
questions.deep: Accuracy = closeness to the true value. Precision = closeness of repeated measurements to each other. A miscalibrated scale can be precise but inaccurate.

questions.why: Line graphs connect data points in order and show trends over time.
questions.deep: Bar graphs compare separate categories, pie charts show parts of a whole, and scatter plots show the relationship between two variables.

questions.why: Unsupported hypotheses are revised, and new experiments are designed to test the revision.
questions.deep: Disproving a hypothesis is useful information. Data should never be discarded or changed to fit a hypothesis.
